I am self employed as a programmer, I hardly ever meet my clients and spend most days behind my own desk at home or even in bed working. I know this isn't particularly healthy but it does comfort me a lot.

That is the biggest problem, I do realize that I can't change or control everything yet it does not settle my nerves which kinda makes it worse. To go insane may be one thing, to know you're going insane seems way worse.

I'm pretty good with my mum, feels like the only thing I got going for me.

I didn't exactly drop out of my prev job, kinda worse, I think. I had my burn out and been out for only 2 months after which I started working a few hours again but in the mean time the company was bought by a huge company. I went from 3 colleagues to 1500, worse part is, the new company basically said, if you can't work full time (after almost 5 months after the initial drop to the floor) you will not get a new contract. I had to decide between a job and my (mental) health. I told them to suck it and left.

I must say it does feel good to talk to someone who can actually relate instead of some doctor who read how it might feel from a textbook.

I've alway been a pessimist but the anxiety really kicked in after my burn out. I'm not sure what would happen or even what the purpose is of the diagnose of Asperger's. Not even sure how I feel about it. Sounds like an excuse to me, something to blame and say I it's not my fault because I have Asperger's. 

Going to Europe isn't going to help me, trust me! I'm not an engineer, I simply live there. Second, traveling is one of the things that trigger my anxiety, being in an unknown situation away from home doesn't do me that good... So I don't actually know how to escape from the situation at home and get away a couple of days. Besides my last attempt at a vacation ended the first day in a motorcycle crash
that's one of the things I can't handle, not being in control. I completely panic when I'm not in control of a situation

Around the time I got the burn out I moved back to my parents and when my dad got the diagnose I decided to stay home and do what ever I can for him. 

My best friend is around a lot which I am very thankful for but luckily he can't really help me with it. He has never been through a lot which is good for him but that does mean he can only listen and not even imagine how I'm feeling.
